column3: Near-verbatim parallel: each self receives what it acquired, within a swift accounting.
Sets non-wronging and recompense only for deeds beside 74:38; the auxiliary contrary route also keeps inward orientation in view.
Frames the self as its own immediate responsibility while retaining a shared return and disclosure of deeds.
Near-verbatim parallel joins each self's acquisition to requital and explicitly excludes misplacement or wronging.
The opening address supplies no direct account, acquisition, or pledge element for 74:38.
Pairs wealth and selves in costly striving; the auxiliary route leaves an inward-intent aspect as a secondary line.
Near-verbatim parallel: every self is requited for acquisition on the accounting day without wronging.
The immediately preceding choice to advance or lag supplies a volitional frame for the following acquired liability.
Self-purification is challenged, adding a contrast between self-claim and non-wronging assessment.
Pairs full payment for each self's acquisition with bringing concealed appropriation forward, extending accountability to what is carried.
The warning-to-humankind frame immediately precedes the self's pledged condition.
The self's formed moral capacity supports a secondary inward-intent reading without defining the pledge image.
Places every self under standing oversight for what it acquired, while retaining both visible speech and inward deception lines.
The command to warn establishes the surrounding summons but no direct account or pledge relation.
Universal self-plus-guardian provides a parallel of retained individual oversight, with an auxiliary inward-record line.
Closest lexical parallel: each person is rahin for what was acquired; the verse also retains family linkage without transferring acquisition.
The stated destination in the local sequence gives consequence context to the pledged-self formulation.
Concrete legal rahn, custody, trust, and testimony supply the collateral register behind rahinah without reducing 74:38 to one register.
Each self knows what it sent ahead and left behind, expanding acquisition into temporal account.
The departing-night oath is local scene-setting only.
Connects recompense to deeds while making its resulting good unknown, a secondary outcome line rather than pledge language.
Each self knows what it brought forward; auxiliary evidence also leaves concealed intent becoming manifest alongside the public account.
Links wrongdoing against oneself with seeking forgiveness, adding a return path without cancelling personal attribution.
The self-reproaching self supplies an inward witness line, with a weaker continuity-of-person line.
Full payment to every self for what it did gives a close, individual, non-reductive account parallel.
The local command of magnification adds no direct account, acquisition, or pledge element.
The universal term is only a distant formal parallel to kullu in 74:38.
Every self arrives with a driver and witness, distinguishing personal presence from evidentiary accompaniment.
The local description of Saqar strengthens consequence context but does not specify why the self is pledged.
The self-directed result of plotting is a useful counterpart; the supplied route remains explicitly contrary rather than preferred support.
Each self argues for itself and is fully paid for its deeds, combining self-concern, individual payment, and non-wronging.
The local sequence shows deliberation and reaction, but provides no direct acquisition or pledge term.
Knowledge of what is within selves supports an inward-condition reading alongside outward acquisition.
Comprehensive inscription provides a record framework for account, though not a self-acquisition formulation.
Directly makes sin-acquisition fall upon one's own self, an important self-binding parallel.
Divine knowledge spans secrecy, openness, and what is acquired, retaining both outward and inward lines.
Deeds being in written records supplies documentary account context without an explicit self or pledge relation.
The local purification command has no direct account or pledge element.
Returning to themselves and recognizing wrong adds an inward self-assessment line.
Return followed by full payment for every self's acquisition closely parallels 74:38 and excludes wronging.
The local address to humanity continues warning context without clarifying the self's acquired pledge.
Universal death and return frame the self's later reckoning but do not state acquisition or pledge.
Every self is requited for what it strives toward, preserving effort as a related but distinct account line.
The moon oath is local scene-setting only.
The tranquil self offers a secondary self-state and return line, not a replacement for acquired liability.
Unfulfilled command is a broad responsibility motif only.
The clear-book opening adds no direct account, acquisition, self, or pledge relation.
Recompense for acquisition gives only a broad outcome parallel.
Explicitly warns that a self can be held fast by what it acquired and that no substitute payment is accepted, closely developing 74:38's pledge image.
The local command to abandon defilement has no direct account or pledge element.
Pairing selves permits both a corresponding-companions line and a weaker record-and-inward-self line.
Gathering and full payment for every self's acquisition closely parallels the individual accounting formula.
The named number over the fire adds local custodial consequence context, not a direct reading of rahinah.
The contrast between what is in a self and exhaustive divine knowledge supports a secondary inward-account line.
Earth's emptying has no direct account, acquisition, self, or pledge relation.
The local depiction of calculating is only indirect context for acquired responsibility.
Change in a people's inward condition precedes change in outward favor, adding a collective inward-condition line.
What hands acquired becomes visible corruption, showing acquisition's outward and shared effects.
The local warning against seeking increase gives only a broad gain-related resonance.
What every self acquires is known despite plotting; the verse retains both concealed-intent and acquired-account lines.
Distinguishes idle utterance from what hearts acquire, supplying a secondary intentionality qualification.
The question about Saqar intensifies the immediate consequence context without interpreting the pledge relation.
Universal witness and recompense are only broad accounting parallels.
Death, testing, and return give a general individual-journey frame for later account.
The local repetition about calculating is indirect context only.
Collective favoring of named figures has no direct account, acquisition, self, or pledge relation.
Each self's acquisition is upon itself and no bearer carries another's burden, establishing non-transferable responsibility.
Writing speech and extending punishment supply record-and-consequence context, without a self-acquisition formula.
Repeated acquisition shapes unjust mutual affiliation, showing a social consequence while retaining personal agency.
Every self tests what it sent ahead before return, a strong temporal-account parallel.
The command of patience for the Lord provides local ethical context but no direct pledge element.
Striving with wealth and selves supports only a secondary costly-action line.
Every self finds good and evil deeds brought present, with desire for distance from evil preserving personal confrontation.
Fire guardians, testing, and hearts' responses give the nearby warning context but no direct acquisition or pledge formula.
Forgetting God is paired with being made to forget one's own selves, adding a sustained self-loss line.
What a self has acquired is for it or against it, while capacity bounds obligation; this qualifies rather than removes attribution.
The dawn oath is local scene-setting only.
Fear within Moses supplies only a narrow inward-state parallel.
Universal selves and the stated outcome give a broad responsibility frame, not a direct acquisition account.
Sealed mouths and witnessing limbs turn what was acquired into bodily evidence, limiting self-defense without displacing attribution.
Breaking a covenant rebounds upon one's own self; auxiliary evidence also preserves inward intention beneath a public act.
A self cannot know tomorrow's acquisition or death-place, keeping personal striving distinct from control of outcomes.
The trumpet blast supplies the immediate transition into the warning and accounting scene.
The call to see signs in selves supports only a general self-attention line.
Every self faces death and receives full wages at resurrection, giving a broad but explicit individual recompense frame.
The declaration of a great warning reinforces nearby consequence context without explaining acquired pledge.
Deception rebounds upon the deceivers' own selves, a self-directed-result parallel.
Benefit requires prior faith or good acquired within it, adding a temporal formation line to what can count for a self.
The night and star-setting instruction is local scene-setting only.
What was acquired fails to avail its holders, contrasting possession or gain with effective release from consequence.
Turning away supplies only a minimal agency contrast.
Change in what is within selves is tied to collective change, supporting inward condition alongside the verse's guardians.
The failure of every obstinate tyrant is only a distant universal-judgment parallel.
Concealed killing and mutual accusation show that distributed blame does not erase disclosure or responsibility.
Guarded scripture, witness, and judgment provide only remote evidentiary context.
The abundance of examples and rejection adds no direct account, acquisition, self, or pledge relation.
The phrase covering every command is only a formal universal-scope parallel.
Imputing what others did not acquire makes the slanderer bear manifest falsehood and sin, sharply preserving proper attribution.
Standing at the Fire and wishing for return gives a consequence-and-regret frame without an explicit acquisition formula.
The self reads its own record and is sufficient as its own reckoner, strongly joining identity, record, and account.
Disclosure or concealment of what is within selves remains subject to account, directly preserving an inward line beside acquired acts.
Each person has a share from what was acquired, adding an acquisition-and-allotment line without the pledge wording.
Whoever does evil is repaid for it and finds no substitute protector or helper, reinforcing non-transferable consequence.
Righteous action with faith is admitted without the slightest wronging, supplying the positive counterpart to individual recompense.
Apparent and concealed sin are both to be left, and what is earned is repaid, preserving parallel outward and inward liability.
Light scales are linked to loss of selves through wronging, giving a self-loss consequence parallel.
What hands sent ahead is tied to consequence while wronging is excluded, supplying an evidentiary-account line.
What was earned is tied to a consequential state, but the verse lacks the self or pledge formulation.
Evil acquisition receives a corresponding evil consequence, a proportional-recompense parallel.
Wronging is denied of God and located in people's wronging of their own selves, sharpening self-directed liability.
Works can receive full worldly payment, adding a temporal recompense contrast to the later pledged-account setting.
The destroyed communities wronged themselves, locating the harmful result in their own agency rather than external injustice.
Each person's deed-record is fastened to the neck and brought forth as an open book, closely extending the self-record line of 17:14.
Guidance or error returns to the guided or erring self, and no bearer carries another's burden, directly reinforcing personal attribution.
Each acts according to an established manner, adding a formed-disposition line to acquisition without fixing its meaning.
The record leaves neither small nor great deed uncounted and confronts each with what was done, while wronging is denied.
One who acts righteously need not fear injustice or diminution, providing a non-wronging recompense parallel.
No self is charged beyond capacity; a truthful record speaks, and wronging is excluded, closely qualifying individual account.
Tongues, hands, and feet testify about what was done, strongly paralleling embodied evidence for acquisition.
Inward certainty alongside outward rejection and self-wronging preserves an inward-intent and self-directed-result line.
A good deed receives what is better and an evil deed only its like, giving proportional requital for what was done.
Striving returns to the striver's own self, a direct self-directed effort parallel.
Each side is not questioned about the other's offense, supporting distinct accountability without the exact acquisition formula.
No burden-bearer carries another's burden, a direct non-transferability parallel to the self held for its own acquisition.
The evils of what was earned befall their earners, showing acquired acts returning as consequence.
Righteous action is for one's self and evil against it; wrongdoing is excluded from the Lord, a close self-directed account parallel.
What hands acquired is tied to affliction while much is pardoned, adding both consequence and non-exhaustive mercy.
Good action is for the self and evil against it, followed by return, directly framing the personal direction of deeds.
Each has degrees from what was done and receives works in full without wronging, a close individual-requital parallel.
No burden-bearer carries another's burden, explicitly preserving non-transferable liability.
A person has only what was striven for, giving a concise effort-and-possession parallel.
Striving will be seen, adding disclosure to the personal effort line.
Striving is then fully repaid, completing the personal effort-account sequence.
Every self is commanded to consider what it sent ahead for tomorrow, closely paralleling acquired liability as forward account.
The self is informed of what it sent ahead and left behind, a close temporal-account parallel.
The self stands as insight or witness against itself, strongly supplementing the personal-account relation.
Even when excuses are offered, the preceding self-witness line remains in force, preserving an evidentiary contrast.
A person sees what hands sent ahead, directly linking embodied action and future confrontation.
Receiving one's record in the right hand introduces an explicit individual record-and-account sequence.
The recipient of the record receives an easy account, directly adding an accounting outcome.
Return to one's people in joy gives a positive post-account outcome line.
Receiving the record from behind introduces the contrary record disposition.
The recipient calls for destruction, giving the adverse account outcome.
The recipient enters a blaze, continuing the adverse record-and-account sequence.
Whoever does an atom's weight of good sees it, making even minimal personal action visible.
Whoever does an atom's weight of evil sees it, completing the minimal-action accountability parallel.
Each community has what it earned and later people have what they earn, supporting distinct rather than inherited acquisition.
The repeated allocation of what each community earned reinforces the non-transferability line across generations.
A person's allotted share from what was earned provides an acquisition-and-recompense parallel.
What hands sent ahead is joined to the exclusion of divine wronging, an anticipatory-account parallel.
One who acquires fault or sin and casts it on an innocent bears manifest falsehood and sin, sharply protecting proper attribution.
The proposal that another return bearing both sins is a contrary liability case, useful for testing rather than overriding the non-transferability line.
Good receives multiplied return and evil only its like, while wronging is excluded, giving proportional personal requital.
Good action is for one's own selves and evil against them, a direct self-directed account parallel.
Hearing, sight, and heart are all questioned, extending responsibility to faculties without an explicit acquisition formula.
Just scales, no wronging to any self, and the smallest deed brought forth make a close accounting parallel.
A record speaks truth about deeds and excludes wronging, supplying documentary-account context.
Light scales are tied to loss of selves, adding an adverse self-loss outcome.
Full payment and manifest knowledge on the day of account strongly reinforce complete disclosure and requital.
No burdened self bears another's burden, reinforcing personal liability within a broader accountability scene.
Wronging is denied of God and located in people wronging themselves, a self-directed liability parallel.
Belief and righteous action erase evil and lead to outcome, a positive remission line alongside personal acquisition.
Strict accounting and severe punishment provide a general account-and-consequence frame.
Death and life are presented as a test of whose action is better, supplying a broad evaluative-action frame.
Presentation leaves no secret concealed, strongly extending the inward-disclosure dimension of account.
The exception for companions of the right supplies an immediate counterpoint to the universal pledged-self statement.
The self's prompting toward evil supplies a distinct inward-disposition line, relevant to the auxiliary weak reading without resolving the pledge image.
